answer: A new agent cannot earn trust alone: it must be vouched for by an established peer that risks part of its own reputation on the newcomer. If the newcomer floods the network with fakes, the voucher loses standing and earning power, so vouching is given sparingly. A Sybil farm then hits a nadir of credibility, because each fake needs a real sponsor willing to risk its name, like timber that only holds weight when its grain is sound. The delta between honest growth and mass fakery becomes visible: genuine agents gain sponsors gradually, while attackers burn sponsor capital at scale.
